╭─ ☤ Hermes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
Correct way: hermes profile delete <profile_name>

It removes the profile directory and any associated Hermes-managed state (routing identity, session mappings, aliases). The -y flag skips the confirmation prompt.

bash
Single profile
hermes profile delete cerebras -y

Multiple profiles
hermes profile delete cerebras gemini-free nvidia-minimaxm3 -y


This is cleaner than rm -rf because it also purges the profile's routing identity from Hermes's internal registry (used for session routing and kanban dispatch).

The old v10 store is at /home/producer32/.local/share/pnpm/store/v10 — not the active store (v11 is current). Since pnpm doesn't manage old version stores, just delete it:

bash
rm -rf /home/producer32/.local/share/pnpm/store/v10


Then prune the active v11 store to remove unreferenced packages:

bash
pnpm store prune


This will free up the v10 store space (likely several GB) plus any orphaned packages in v11.
